sanskrit: rājataḥ salilād agneś corataḥ svajanād api bhayam arthavatāṃ nityaṃ mṛtyoḥ prāṇabhṛtām iva
english: The wealthy live in constant fear — from kings, from water, from fire, from thieves, from kinsmen — just as all living beings dwell in fear of death.

sanskrit: yathā hy āmiṣam ākāśe pakṣibhiḥ śvāpadair bhuvi bhakṣyate salile matsyais tathā sarveṇa vittavān
english: Just as flesh in the sky is devoured by birds, on land by beasts, in water by fish — so in every sphere is the wealthy man devoured.

sanskrit: artha eva hi keṣāṃ cid anartho bhavitā nṛṇām arthāśreyasi cāsakto na śreyo vindate naraḥ tasmād arthāgamāḥ sarve manomohavivardhanāḥ
english: For some men wealth itself becomes misfortune. One attached to wealth as the highest good never attains the highest good. Therefore all gains of wealth only deepen the delusion of the mind.

sanskrit: kārpaṇyaṃ darpamānau ca bhayam udvega eva ca arthajāni viduḥ prājñā duḥkhāny etāni dehinām
english: Meanness, arrogance, pride, fear, and anxiety — the wise know these miseries of embodied beings to be born of wealth.

sanskrit: arthasyopārjane duḥkhaṃ pālane ca kṣaye tathā nāśe duḥkhaṃ vyaye duḥkhaṃ ghnanti caivārthakāraṇāt
english: There is suffering in earning wealth, suffering in guarding it and in its diminishment; suffering in its loss, suffering in its expenditure — and men even kill one another on account of wealth.

sanskrit: arthā duḥkhaṃ parityaktuṃ pālitāś cāpi te 'sukhāḥ duḥkhena cādhigamyante teṣāṃ nāśaṃ na cintayet
english: Riches are painful to relinquish, and even when guarded bring no happiness; they are acquired with suffering — therefore one should not grieve at their loss.

sanskrit: asaṃtoṣaparā mūḍhāḥ saṃtoṣaṃ yānti paṇḍitāḥ anto nāsti pipāsāyāḥ saṃtoṣaḥ paramaṃ sukham
english: The foolish pursue dissatisfaction; the wise attain contentment. Thirst has no end — contentment is the highest happiness.

sanskrit: tasmāt saṃtoṣam eveha dhanaṃ paśyanti paṇḍitāḥ anityaṃ yauvanaṃ rūpaṃ jīvitaṃ dravyasaṃcayaḥ aiśvaryaṃ priyasaṃvāso gṛdhyed eṣu na paṇḍitaḥ
english: Therefore the wise regard contentment itself as wealth in this world. Youth, beauty, life, accumulation of goods, lordship, and the company of loved ones — all are impermanent; the wise person should not covet these.

sanskrit: tyajeta saṃcayāṃs tasmāt tajjaṃ kleśaṃ saheta kaḥ na hi saṃcayavān kaś cid dṛśyate nirupadravaḥ
english: Therefore one should abandon hoarding — who could endure the distress born of it? For no one who accumulates is ever seen to be free from affliction.

sanskrit: ataś ca dharmibhiḥ pumbhir anīhārthaḥ praśasyate prakṣālanād dhi paṅkasya dūrād asparśanaṃ varam
english: Hence virtuous men praise freedom from desire for wealth. Indeed, it is better not to touch mire at all than to wash it off afterward.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraivam artheṣu na spṛhāṃ kartum arhasi dharmeṇa yadi te kāryaṃ vimukteccho bhavārthataḥ
english: O Yudhiṣṭhira, you should not hanker after possessions in this way. If you wish to act in accordance with dharma and desire liberation from the cycle of existence, act with that intent.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca nārthopabhogalipsārtham iyam arthepsutā mama bharaṇārthaṃ tu viprāṇāṃ brahman kāṅkṣe na lobhataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This desire for wealth in me is not for the sake of enjoying riches. O brahmin, I seek it only to maintain the brahmins — not out of greed.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hy asmadvidho brahman vartamāno gṛhāśrame bharaṇaṃ pālanaṃ cāpi na kuryād anuyāyinām
english: How could one like me, living in the householder's stage of life, fail to provide for and protect those who follow him, O brahmin?

sanskrit: saṃvibhāgo hi bhūtānāṃ sarveṣām eva śiṣyate tathaivāpacamānebhyaḥ pradeyaṃ gṛhamedhinā
english: For the householder, sharing with all beings remains an obligation; likewise, food is to be given to those who come to eat.

sanskrit: tṛṇāni bhūmir udakaṃ vāk caturthī ca sūnṛtā satām etāni geheṣu nocchidyante kadā cana
english: Grass, ground, water, and as the fourth, kind and truthful speech — these things in the homes of the good are never exhausted at any time.

sanskrit: deyam ārtasya śayanaṃ sthitaśrāntasya cāsanam tṛṣitasya ca pānīyaṃ kṣudhitasya ca bhojanam
english: A bed should be given to the distressed, a seat to one standing and weary, water to the thirsty, and food to the hungry.

sanskrit: cakṣur dadyān mano dadyād vācaṃ dadyāc ca sūnṛtām pratyudgamyābhigamanaṃ kuryān nyāyena cārcanam
english: One should offer one's eyes, one's mind, and truthful speech; one should go forward to receive a guest, and offer homage in the proper manner.

sanskrit: aghihotram anaḍvāṃś ca jñātayo 'tithibāndhavāḥ putradārabhṛtāś caiva nirdaheyur apūjitāḥ
english: The sacred fire, the draft ox, kinsmen, guests, relatives, sons, wife, and servants — if left unhonoured, they would burn a man as surely as fire.

sanskrit: nātmārthaṃ pācayed annaṃ na vṛthā ghātayet paśūn na ca tat svayam aśnīyād vidhivad yan na nirvapet
english: One should not cook food for oneself alone, nor slaughter animals in vain, nor eat for oneself what one has not properly offered according to the rites.

sanskrit: śvabhyaś ca śvapacebhyaś ca vayobhyaś cāvaped bhuvi vaiśvadevaṃ hi nāmaitat sāyaṃprātar vidhīyate
english: One should cast food on the ground for dogs, for outcastes, and for birds — this is the Vaiśvadeva rite, prescribed to be performed morning and evening.

sanskrit: vighasāśī bhavet tasmān nityaṃ cāmṛtabhojanaḥ vighasaṃ bhṛtyaśeṣaṃ tu yajñaśeṣaṃ tathāmṛtam
english: Therefore one should always eat only the remnants left by others, and partake of what is like nectar — remnants left by servants are vighasam, and remnants of sacrifice are amṛtam.

sanskrit: etāṃ yo vartate vṛttiṃ vartamāno gṛhāśrame tasya dharmaṃ paraṃ prāhuḥ kathaṃ vā vipra manyase
english: They say that one who lives in the householder's stage following this mode of conduct upholds the highest dharma. What, O brahmin, do you think of this?

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca aho bata mahat kaṣṭaṃ viparītam idaṃ jagat yenāpatrapate sādhur asādhus tena tuṣyati
english: Śaunaka said: Alas, how great is the hardship, and how inverted is this world — that by which the virtuous man is ashamed, by that very thing the wicked man is pleased.

sanskrit: śiśnodarakṛte 'prājñaḥ karoti vighasaṃ bahu moharāgasamākrānta indriyārthavaśānugaḥ
english: The unwise man, overpowered by delusion and passion, enslaved to the objects of the senses, accumulates great quantities of food-remnants for the sake of belly and genitals.

sanskrit: hriyate budhyamāno 'pi naro hāribhir indriyaiḥ vimūḍhasaṃjño duṣṭāśvair udbhrāntair iva sārathiḥ
english: Even a man who knows is carried away by his enticing senses, bewildered in understanding, like a charioteer dragged off by runaway, vicious horses.

sanskrit: ṣaḍindriyāṇi viṣayaṃ samāgacchanti vai yadā tadā prādurbhavaty eṣāṃ pūrvasaṃkalpajaṃ manaḥ
english: When the six senses come together with their objects, then the mind — born of prior intention — manifests among them.

sanskrit: mano yasyendriyagrāmaviṣayaṃ prati coditam tasyautsukyaṃ saṃbhavati pravṛttiś copajāyate
english: In one whose mind is urged toward the objects of the group of senses, restlessness arises and activity is born.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃkalpavīryeṇa kāmena viṣayeṣubhiḥ viddhaḥ patati lobhāgnau jyotir lobhāt pataṃgavat
english: Then, pierced by desire — the power of intention — and by the sense objects, he falls into the fire of greed, just as a moth falls into flame out of craving for light.

sanskrit: tato vihārair āhārair mohitaś ca viśāṃ pate mahāmohamukhe magno nātmānam avabudhyate
english: Then, O lord of the people, deluded by pleasures and food, plunged into the mouth of great delusion, he no longer knows himself.

sanskrit: evaṃ patati saṃsāre tāsu tāsv iha yoniṣu avidyākarmatṛṣṇābhir bhrāmyamāṇo 'tha cakravat
english: Thus he falls into saṃsāra, wandering through these various wombs, driven round and round like a wheel by ignorance, karma, and thirst.

sanskrit: brahmādiṣu tṛṇānteṣu hūteṣu parivartate jale bhuvi tathākāśe jāyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: He revolves through existences from Brahmā down to a blade of grass, being born again and again in water, on land, and in the sky.

sanskrit: abudhānāṃ gatis tv eṣā budhānām api me śṛṇu ye dharme śreyasi ratā vimokṣaratayo janāḥ
english: This is the path of the unwise; now hear from me the path of the wise — those who delight in dharma and the highest good, who are devoted to liberation.

sanskrit: yad idaṃ vedavacanaṃ kuru karma tyajeti ca tasmād dharmān imān sarvān nābhimānāt samācaret
english: The Vedic injunction says both 'perform action' and 'renounce action' — therefore one should perform all these dharmic duties not out of pride or self-regard.

sanskrit: ijyādhyayanadānāni tapaḥ satyaṃ kṣamā damaḥ alobha iti mārgo 'yaṃ dharmasyāṣṭavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Sacrifice, study, giving, austerity, truthfulness, forbearance, restraint, and non-greed — this eightfold path is remembered as the way of dharma.

sanskrit: tatra pūrvaś caturvargaḥ pitṛyānapathe sthitaḥ kartavyam iti yat kāryaṃ nābhimānāt samācaret
english: Of these, the first four belong to the path of the ancestors; whatever must be done should be performed as a duty, not out of pride.

sanskrit: uttaro devayānas tu sadbhir ācaritaḥ sadā aṣṭāṅgenaiva mārgeṇa viśuddhātmā samācaret
english: The latter four constitute the path of the gods, always practised by the virtuous; one with a purified soul should follow this eightfold path.

sanskrit: samyak saṃkalpasaṃbandhāt samyak cendriyanigrahāt samyag vrataviśeṣāc ca samyak ca gurusevanāt
english: Through right intention, right restraint of the senses, right observance of special vows, and right service to a teacher —

sanskrit: samyag āhārayogāc ca samyak cādhyayanāgamāt samyak karmopasaṃnyāsāt samyak cittanirodhanāt evaṃ karmāṇi kurvanti saṃsāravijigīṣavaḥ
english: — through right discipline in food, right adherence to scriptural study, right renunciation of action, and right restraint of the mind — thus those who wish to conquer saṃsāra perform their actions.

sanskrit: rāgadveṣavinirmuktā aiśvaryaṃ devatā gatāḥ rudrāḥ sādhyās tathādityā vasavo 'thāśvināv api yogaiśvaryeṇa saṃyuktā dhārayanti prajā imāḥ
english: Free from passion and aversion, they attain the sovereignty of the gods — the Rudras, the Sādhyas, the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Aśvins — who, endowed with the power of yoga, uphold these living beings.

sanskrit: tathā tvam api kaunteya śamam āsthāya puṣkalam tapasā siddhim anviccha yogasiddhiṃ ca bhārata
english: Likewise, O son of Kuntī, taking firm hold of supreme tranquility, seek perfection through austerity, and the perfection of yoga, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: pitṛmātṛmayī siddhiḥ prāptā karmamayī ca te tapasā siddhim anviccha dvijānāṃ bharaṇāya vai
english: The perfection born of father and mother has been attained by you, and that born of action too — now seek perfection through austerity, truly for the sake of maintaining the twice-born.

sanskrit: siddhā hi yad yad icchanti kurvate tad anugrahāt tasmāt tapaḥ samāsthāya kuruṣvātmamanoratham
english: For the perfected ones, whatever they desire they accomplish through their grace. Therefore, taking recourse to austerity, fulfil the desire of your heart.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śaunakenaivam uktas tu kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ purohitam upāgamya bhrātṛmadhye 'bravīd idam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having been thus addressed by Śaunaka, Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, approached the family priest Dhaumya and spoke these words in the midst of his brothers.

sanskrit: prasthitaṃ mānuyāntīme brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ na cāsmi pālane śakto bahuduḥkhasamanvitaḥ
english: These brahmin masters of the Vedas are setting out to follow me wherever I go, and I am not capable of maintaining them, afflicted as I am with great suffering.

sanskrit: parityaktuṃ na śaknomi dānaśaktiś ca nāsti me katham atra mayā kāryaṃ bhagavāṃs tad bravītu me
english: I cannot abandon them, and yet I have no power to give. Revered one, tell me what I ought to do in this matter.

sanskrit: muhūrtam iva sa dhyātvā dharmeṇānviṣya tāṃ gatim yudhiṣṭhiram uvācedaṃ dhaumyo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Pondering for a moment and searching for the right course through dharma, Dhaumya — foremost among upholders of righteousness — spoke these words to Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: purā sṛṣṭāni bhūtāni pīḍyante kṣudhayā bhṛśam tato 'nukampayā teṣāṃ savitā svapitā iva
english: In primordial times, when all created beings were greatly tormented by hunger, the Sun, out of compassion for them, became like their own father.

sanskrit: gatvottarāyaṇaṃ tejorasān uddhṛtya raśmibhiḥ dakṣiṇāyanam āvṛtto mahīṃ niviśate raviḥ
english: Having gone to the northern course and drawn up the essence of light with his rays, the Sun returns on the southern course and pours it into the earth.

sanskrit: kṣetrabhūte tatas tasminn oṣadhīr oṣadhīpatiḥ divas tejaḥ samuddhṛtya janayām āsa vāriṇā
english: Then the Moon, lord of herbs, the earth having become the field, drawing up the celestial radiance and combining it with water, generates the herbs.

sanskrit: niṣiktaś candratejobhiḥ sūyate bhūgato raviḥ oṣadhyaḥ ṣaḍrasā medhyās tadannaṃ prāṇināṃ bhuvi
english: The Sun, resting in the earth and infused with the light of the Moon, gives birth to the herbs endowed with six tastes and purifying qualities — that is the food of living beings on earth.

sanskrit: evaṃ bhānumayaṃ hy annaṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇadhāraṇam pitaiṣa sarvabhūtānāṃ tasmāt taṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja
english: Thus is food made of solar light the sustainer of life for all beings. He is the father of all beings — therefore take refuge in him.

sanskrit: rājāno hi mahātmāno yonikarmaviśodhitāḥ uddharanti prajāḥ sarvās tapa āsthāya puṣkalam
english: For great-souled kings, purified by birth and action, uplift all their subjects by taking recourse to abundant austerity.

sanskrit: bhīmena kārtavīryeṇa vainyena nahuṣeṇa ca tapoyogasamādhisthair uddhṛtā hy āpadaḥ prajāḥ
english: By Bhīmasena, by Kārtavīrya, by Vainya, and by Nahuṣa — all abiding in the absorption of austerity and yoga — were the subjects rescued from calamities.

sanskrit: tathā tvam api dharmātman karmaṇā ca viśodhitaḥ tapa āsthāya dharmeṇa dvijātīn bhara bhārata
english: Likewise, O righteous one, you too are purified by your deeds — taking recourse to austerity and dharma, sustain the twice-born, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu dhaumyena tat kālasadṛśaṃ vacaḥ dharmarājo viśuddhātmā tapa ātiṣṭhad uttamam
english: Thus addressed by Dhaumya with words befitting that time, the king of dharma, pure in soul, undertook supreme austerity.

sanskrit: puṣpopahārair balibhir arcayitvā divākaram yogam āsthāya dharmātmā vāyubhakṣo jitendriyaḥ gāṅgeyaṃ vāry upaspṛṣya prāṇāyāmena tasthivān
english: Having worshipped the Sun with offerings of flowers and oblations, the dharma-souled one took his yoga posture, subsisting on air alone, with senses conquered, touching the waters of the Ganges, and stood firm in prāṇāyāma.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kathaṃ kurūṇām ṛṣabhaḥ sa tu rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ viprārtham ārādhitavān sūryam adbhutavikramam
english: Janamejaya said: How did that king Yudhiṣṭhira, the bull of the Kurus, propitiate the Sun of wondrous power for the sake of the brahmins?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājañ śucir bhūtvā samāhitaḥ kṣaṇaṃ ca kuru rājendra sarvaṃ vakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Listen attentively, O king — become pure and composed, and for a moment be still, O lord of kings. I shall recount everything without remainder.

sanskrit: dhaumyena tu yatha proktaṃ pārthāya sumahātmane nāmnām aṣṭaśataṃ puṇyaṃ tac chṛṇuṣva mahāmate
english: As recited by Dhaumya to the greatly noble son of Pṛthā — hear those holy one hundred and eight names, O greatly wise one.

sanskrit: sūryo 'ryamā bhagas tvaṣṭā pūṣārkaḥ savitā raviḥ gabhastimān ajaḥ kālo mṛtyur dhātā prabhākaraḥ
english: Sūrya, Aryaman, Bhaga, Tvaṣṭā, Pūṣan, Arka, Savitā, Ravi, Gabhastimān, Aja, Kāla, Mṛtyu, Dhātā, Prabhākara —

sanskrit: pṛthivy āpaś ca tejaś ca khaṃ vāyuś ca parāyaṇam somo bṛhaspatiḥ śukro budho 'ṅgāraka eva ca
english: Earth, Water, Fire, Sky, Wind, the Supreme Refuge, Soma, Bṛhaspati, Śukra, Budha, and Aṅgāraka —

sanskrit: indro vivasvān dīptāṃśuḥ śuciḥ śauriḥ śanaiścaraḥ brahmā viṣṇuś ca rudraś ca skando vaiśravaṇo yamaḥ
english: Indra, Vivasvān, Dīptāṃśu, Śuci, Śauri, Śanaiścara, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Skanda, Vaiśravaṇa, Yama —

sanskrit: vaidyuto jāṭharaś cāgnir aindhanas tejasāṃ patiḥ dharmadhvajo vedakartā vedāṅgo vedavāhanaḥ
english: The fire of lightning, the digestive fire, the fire of fuel, Lord of luminosities, Dharmadhvaja, Creator of the Vedas, Vedic limb, Bearer of the Vedas —

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaś ca kaliḥ sarvāmarāśrayaḥ kalā kāṣṭhā muhūrtāś ca pakṣā māsā ṛtus tathā
english: Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, Kali, Refuge of all immortals, the kaḷā, the kāṣṭhā, the muhūrtas, the fortnights, the months, and the seasons —

sanskrit: saṃvatsarakaro 'śvatthaḥ kālacakro vibhāvasuḥ puruṣaḥ śāśvato yogī vyaktāvyaktaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Maker of the year, the Aśvattha tree, the Wheel of Time, Vibhāvasu, the Eternal Person, the Yogi, the Manifest and Unmanifest, the Eternal —

sanskrit: lokādhyakṣaḥ prajādhyakṣo viśvakarmā tamonudaḥ varuṇaḥ sāgaro 'ṃśuś ca jīmūto jīvano 'rihā
english: Overseer of the worlds, Overseer of creatures, Viśvakarmā, Dispeller of darkness, Varuṇa, the Ocean, Ray of light, Cloud, Giver of life, Slayer of enemies —

sanskrit: bhūtāśrayo bhūtapatiḥ sarvabhūtaniṣevitaḥ maṇiḥ suvarṇo bhūtādiḥ kāmadaḥ sarvatomukhaḥ
english: Refuge of beings, Lord of beings, Worshipped by all beings, the Jewel, Gold, Origin of beings, Granter of desires, Facing all directions —

sanskrit: jayo viśālo varadaḥ śīghragaḥ prāṇadhāraṇaḥ dhanvantarir dhūmaketur ādidevo 'diteḥ sutaḥ
english: Victory, the Vast, Bestower of boons, Swift-moving, Sustainer of life-breath, Dhanvantari, Dhūmaketu, the Primordial God, Son of Aditi —

sanskrit: dvādaśātmāravindākṣaḥ pitā mātā pitāmahaḥ svargadvāraṃ prajādvāraṃ mokṣadvāraṃ triviṣṭapam
english: Twelve-natured, Lotus-eyed, Father, Mother, Grandsire, Gate of heaven, Gate of creatures, Gate of liberation, the Triple Heaven —

sanskrit: dehakartā praśāntātmā viśvātmā viśvatomukhaḥ carācarātmā sūkṣmātmā maitreṇa vapuṣānvitaḥ
english: Maker of bodies, the Tranquil Soul, Soul of the universe, Facing all the world, Soul of moving and unmoving things, the Subtle Soul, endowed with a form of friendliness —

sanskrit: etad vai kīrtanīyasya sūryasyaiva mahātmanaḥ nāmnām aṣṭaśataṃ puṇyaṃ śakreṇoktaṃ mahātmanā
english: This indeed is the sacred set of one hundred and eight names of the great-souled Sun who is to be glorified, as proclaimed by the great-souled Indra.

sanskrit: śakrāc ca nāradaḥ prāpto dhaumyaś ca tadanantaram dhaumyād yudhiṣṭhiraḥ prāpya sarvān kāmān avāptavān
english: Nārada received this from Indra, and Dhaumya received it next from Nārada; having received it from Dhaumya, Yudhiṣṭhira attained all his desires.

sanskrit: surapitṛgaṇayakṣasevitaṃ; hy asuraniśācarasiddhavanditam varakanakahutāśanaprabhaṃ; tvam api manasy abhidhehi bhāskaram
english: Attended upon by the hosts of gods and ancestral spirits and yakṣas, worshipped by asuras, night-wanderers, and siddhas, radiant as choice gold and blazing fire — hold the Sun also in your mind.

sanskrit: sūryodaye yas tu samāhitaḥ paṭhet; sa putralābhaṃ dhanaratnasaṃcayān labheta jātismaratāṃ sadā naraḥ; smṛtiṃ ca medhāṃ ca sa vindate parām
english: One who recites this at sunrise with a composed mind will gain sons, accumulate wealth and gems, always attain the memory of past births, and find supreme memory and intellect.

sanskrit: imaṃ stavaṃ devavarasya yo naraḥ; prakīrtayec chucisumanāḥ samāhitaḥ sa mucyate śokadavāgnisāgarāl; labheta kāmān manasā yathepsitān
english: The person who glorifies this hymn of the best of gods, pure and clear-minded, with concentrated thought, shall be released from the ocean of the wildfire of grief, and shall attain all desires as wished for in the heart.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato divākaraḥ prīto darśayām āsa pāṇḍavam dīpyamānaḥ svavapuṣā jvalann iva hutāśanaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the Sun, well pleased, appeared before the son of Pāṇḍu, blazing with his own radiance, burning like a sacrificial fire.

sanskrit: yat te 'bhilaṣitaṃ rājan sarvam etad avāpsyasi aham annaṃ pradāsyāmi sapta pañca ca te samāḥ
english: "O king, you shall obtain everything you have desired. I shall grant you food for twelve years — five and seven."

sanskrit: phalamūlāmiṣaṃ śākaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ yan mahānase caturvidhaṃ tadannādyam akṣayyaṃ te bhaviṣyati dhanaṃ ca vividhaṃ tubhyam ity uktvāntaradhīyata
english: "Fruits, roots, flesh, and vegetables — the fourfold food prepared in your kitchen shall be inexhaustible for you, and various wealth as well." Having said this, the Sun disappeared.

sanskrit: labdhvā varaṃ tu kaunteyo jalād uttīrya dharmavit jagrāha pādau dhaumyasya bhrātṝṃś cāsvajatācyutaḥ
english: Having received the boon, the son of Kuntī, the knower of dharma, rose from the water, clasped the feet of Dhaumya, and the unwavering one embraced his brothers.

sanskrit: draupadyā saha saṃgamya paśyamāno 'bhyayāt prabhuḥ mahānase tadānnaṃ tu sādhayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: The lord met with Draupadī, and then, as all watched, the son of Pāṇḍu went and had the food in the kitchen prepared.
